## Stag Falls

Stag Falls was a small village nestled in the mountains near Ravens Bluff during the mid-to-late 14 century DR.

Geography
The area was nestled between mountains.

Government
Stag Falls was a barony, and its baron recognized the mayor of Ravens Bluff as their liege.

Trade
Of note, the village exported furs, and star rose quartz from nearby streams. Its taxes were paid in furs, wool, and fur/wool products.

Defenses
There was a castle.

History
Centuries before the mid-to-late 14 century DR, the castle in the future site of Stag Falls was attacked and destroyed by hosts opposing the vampire wizard Romanisk Vlaensk. Unable to pursue him effectively into the foundations and tunnels underneath, the hosts settled instead for collapsing the castle to prevent him from escaping. The vampire decided to bide his time underground, researching sorcery.

The village and castle were resettled and rebuilt by Karl von Stag Falls, the grand-grandfather of Vilhelm von Stag Falls. In the mid-to-late 14 century DR, baron Vilhelm ran the barony as a protectorate of Ravens Bluff, recognizing the Mayor as his liege. The village came to prosper from trade with the Bluff.

Nearly a decade into Baron Vilhelm's reign, he became curious about the history of the area, and had dwarves dig into the foundations of his castle; over the course of a year, they finally found the chambers beneath. Unfortunately, their digging released the vampire Romanisk Vlaensk, who slew them all and turned the Baron into an undead thrall. The Baron in turn was charged with terrorizing the village, in preparation for the vampire's further schemes.

The vampire's actions prevented the village's taxes from being paid, which in turn prompted investigation from Ravens Bluff; Field General Marcus Rubicon sent a patrol, which never reported nor returned. About a month after the vampire's release, the man sent a small detail of adventurers instead.

Along the way, those adventurers learned the trail was muddy, though passable, and spoke to other travelers, learning no one had come from Stag Falls; on the muddy trail, they found the patrol, torn apart by wolves. They were then attacked by extremely rare werebats and a pack of wolves; they found the farms near Stag Falls uninhabited, yet sowed, and the blades of all farm tools taken at the Latimer farm, and the Haldine farm thoroughly ransacked. The shrine of Chauntea was abandoned, with the altar service missing, and the Church of Torm dilapidated and desecrated. A maiden had committed suicide in one of the homes, and a boy had been killed for freeing all the dogs from their kennels. The first live person they encountered was a young man, Tommy Fletcher, a shepherd; he was heavily injured, and only survived thanks to their aid, taking them to the nearby caves, where the people had fled the Baron, led by the priestess of Chauntea, a woman named Sidone. Rather than return to Ravens Bluff for aid, the adventurers decided to spend the night in the caves and search further in the morning.

On the morning, they helped deliver a child; Sidone explained she was late, because she'd been searching for two youths, Kitarno and Lyra; she wished the adventurers luck, and offered them a ring of spell storing. On their path to the castle, the adventurers came across them shortly after, discovering the boy believed she'd been bit by a vampire, and in the process of torching her body. They were able to prevent this and heal the two of them; finally at the castle, they discovered the Baron had been turned into an undead, and that he had taken mental control of almost the entire castle staff. Managing to defeat him in battle, the adventurers pursued his master, the vampire Romanisk Vlaensk, into the underground.

## Steam Clashes

The Steam Clashes, Steam War, or Ajhuutal Mutiny was a short war between between the great genie Calim and his rebellious vassal Ajhuu, pitting the Calim Empire against the Maridlands. It ended in the Shattering, a vast magical earthquake that destroyed and sank much of the region.

Description
In, Calim was forced to halt his empire's expansion and make peace with the elves of Tethir and Darthiir Wood, and the dwarves of Shanatar, fixing his borders at the River Agis and Alimir Mountains (the implication being that they had produced an incredible measure to threaten him with). In order to secure the peace further, he performed them the "service" of exterminating the giants and dragons that lived in the Marching Mountains. This military campaign took his full attention, meaning that he did not realize the dissatisfaction his reduced imperial ambitions was causing in his court.

Perhaps following the example set by the recent rebellion of other marids and their formation of the Marid States in the Sea of Fallen Stars, the marid lord Ajhuu claimed the easternmost portion of Calim's empire while he was distracted, and founded his capital of Ajhuutal. It took until  for Calim to return from his campaigns and redirect his focus on his former vassal, prompting a series of devastating battles that failed to prove a victor. Ajhuu's lieutenants Haj and Luar were either slain or bound in the course of these battles, and it was believed that the site of it became Hajluar's Falls and the Maridflow river.

Calim's subjects noticed that Ajhuu's realm was far more free and egalitarian than their own, and this began to produce more internal dissension. Unwilling to tolerate any further appearance of weakness in his empire, in  Calim gathered his dao allies and his magical artifacts from the Great Arrival, and used them to destroy Ajhuutal. In an event called the Shattering, the spell caused an immense earthquake that destroyed Ajhuu, his capital, and the land it stood on, sending the remains into the Shining Sea. Calim's zealousness in pursuing an overpowering victory meant that the earthquake then spread along the coast, sinking vast regions of his own empire and permanently altering the coastline. Though the price had been high, Calim ultimately ended the Ajhuutal Mutiny and secured peace for his empire, at least until the arrival of Memnon in .

Ajhuutal remained a figure of fascination for the future inhabitants of Calimshan, though it was confused with an unrelated ruined site that was dubbed Lost Ajhuutal.

## Starnar's Cozy Cove Rest

Starnar's Cozy Cove Rest was a ramshackle tavern and inn, a notable step down from Tulmene's Tower, located in the Tethyrean town Tulmene on Cape Velen in the late 14 century DR.

Interior
Starnar's establishment and most all what was inside was shabby and patched or mended. Vermin was a frequent sight in the inn, but it was recommended to the guests to avoid pointing rats and mice to the staff, unless the guest wanted a dubious entertainment of watching young unwashed women throwing daggers at the scurrying rodents.

Services
Starnar's Cozy Cove Rest offered lodgings to those who could not afford to pay for beds in Tulmene's Tower. The rooms came with fresh linens and pillows, but, unless requested, the said rooms were sparsely furnished if at all. As for the dining experience, the Rest had little to offer, apart from black bread to be dipped in large bubbling cauldrons of heavily-spiced thick hog stew. By some accounts and evident by the beaks found in the crocks, the stew was a collection of "every dead bird they could gather." Despite that, both the stew and the bread on offer were quite tasty. Lastly, when the catch of the day came into Tulmene's harbors, the inn served fresh pan-fried fish that ranged from a single copper to a single silver piece. The hose beer on tap was back in color, thick, and packed a wallop with a hint of saltiness. Strong beer was a welcome sight among all the watered-down drinks served in many dockside watering holes.

Inhabitants
In the 14 century DR, the inn was run by a crippled retired sailor named Starnar, who was forced into the profession by the need to support his nine or ten daughters (Volothamp Geddarm, when describing the establishment, lost track of the exact number of daughters). Starnar's man-craized daughters were the inn's staff and attracted a large number of sailors and other, more shady individuals, like pirates. Many of these guests heard of the daughters' needs for husbands and tried to woo the young women during their stay.

## Stalwart Knights

The Stalwart Knights was a Helmite order of warriors and priests that comprised an entire division of the Champions Vigilant and, at some point before the late 14 century DR, served as the city guard and later a police force in the town of Velen in Tethyr and its surrounding lads.

Organization
The Stalwart Knights were based out of The Home of the Stalwarts, a temple dedicated to Helm, located in the town of Velen on the Dragon's Head Peninsula. The organization consisted of 100 priests and 50 warriors circa 1370 DR. The Chevangard often exchanged its members with both warriors and priests of the Stalwart Knights. The Stalwart Knights performed numerous pompous rituals, one of which was the change of guard at The Home of the Stalwarts, done four times a day. Notably, one of these guard changes was called the Vigil, when fully armored knights lined the temple's battlements to watch the passage and the setting of the sun.

History
The Home of the Stalwarts was a historic structure in Velen and was considered by many to be "the anchor on which Velen was built." The Stalwart Knights served as Velen's guards and militia, protecting the city from the constant looming threat of pirates. This protection of the city allowed Velen to grow and prosper. By the late 14 century DR, the Stalwart Knights kept peace in the lands adjacent to Velen, protecting them from thieves, smugglers, pirates, and brigands. Locals believed that the Stalwart Knights were the only thing that stopped the thieves' guilds from taking over Velen.

Members
Circa 1370 DR, the Stalwart Knights, as well as the lay-members of the temple, were led by Overblade Orrdun Fistright, a warrior-priest of Helm, who inherited the position from the  locally much-beloved Orm Talath.

## Stormreach

Stormreach was a city in the world of Eberron, located on the continent of Xen'drik. It was the main port of the continent, and dominated by the political and mercantile interests of the great Houses Jorasco, Phiarlan, Kundarak, and Deneith, while also being home to the devout priests of the Silver Flame, the druidic Gatekeepers, and the arcane sages of the Twelve.

History
Around the time of Faerûn's Darkening in the 1480s DR, the Lords of Dust hidden in the city enacted a scheme to find and free the Spinner of Shadows, a powerful demonic Overlord trapped in Khyber beneath the city. Led by figures such as Gnomon, Karas, and Sabriz Rinzyn Kho, they opened the road to Tarath Marad and broke into the Spinner's Prison, weakening the Silver Flame Guardian enough that the Spinner was able to call out to Lolth. Instead of rampaging into Eberron to free the other Overlords and take over the world, the Spinner escaped through the Rift Between Worlds and delivered a large quantity of dragonshards to Lolth before being voluntarily consumed by the goddess.

The Church of the Silver Flame, the Gatekeepers, and the Twelve all came to address the open portal that led into the Demonweb Pits, leading to them sending a team of heroes through it to find a solution. Those heroes went on to meet Elminster and found their way to Eveningstar in Cormyr, helping to defeat Lolth's plans to conquer Mystra's Weave and saving Eberron in the process.

## Sturge Whitsunday

Sturge Whitsunday was a paladin and politician of Selgaunt, from the prominent Whitsunday family. He was tapped for a political mission to find Myth Nantar in .

Description
Standing  tall and weighing, he had fair skin, blond hair, blue eyes.

Personality
He was always ready with a glad hand and a welcome greeting, but often came off as just too slick for comfort. He was somewhat sensitive about his own physical clumsiness.

Abilities
Sturge was an excellent rider, and could hold his own at heraldry and bureaucracy both Sembian and elven. Even for a paladin, he was quite charismatic.

He also spoke elven.

Possessions
He bore, of note, an enchanted chain mail, a short sword of quickness, and a philter of persuasiveness. Curiously he also carried a ceremonial gold-lace coif (skull cap), and a full compliment of grooming accessories, including razor, mirror, towel, basin, two different formal tunics, a formal sleeveless surcoat, a silken full cape, leather belt, felt cap. Presumably, he didn't wear all of them at once.

Activities
Sturge Whitsunday had joined the Diplomatic Corps of Selgaunt right out of academy.

Relationships
He was the oldest child of the Whitsunday family. His younger sister was Aleine Whitsunday; their father was dead, and he believed she'd never disobey him like she was doing if he lived.

Of their possible companions, he thought Nagreous Twiddle was a national treasure, though he was trying on the nerves, and would have to be allowed to speak if engineering matters came to the fore. He looked down on Rondo Marsh, whom he thought of as nothing but a commoner understandably hating him for his high birth; he deferred to captain Coprates Bile, though he was not opposed to showing her, in private, how a real lady ought to act. He found Ilsa Merrymore to be stunning, but while he hoped to win her over, foremost in his mind was worrying about how to keep her from speaking out of turn when dealing with foreign emissaries.

History
Sturge Whitsunday was the oldest brother of the prominent Whitsunday family, and he joined the Diplomatic Corps straight out of the academy. In, he brokered a renegotiated deal with the Elven Court on behalf of Sembia, earning him an appointment by the Mayor, Andeth Ilchammar, to a new assignment on Mirtul of the next year: to find a hidden city of aquatic elves (actually Myth Nantar), and broker a deal with them, too.

If he failed, things would look grim for him come election season. If he succeeded, he'd get an enchanted conch to call the forces of Myth Nantar to the aid of Selgaunt.

Rumors & Legends
Though Sturge believed he'd been tapped, naturally, for his diplomatic skills, this was true in a different way than he thought - he was selected in hopes that he'd die in the mission, eliminating the able diplomat as a potential rival for mayor Andeth Ilchammar.
